dedupe_keys.name: fsb format for incident reporting exchange fire taxonomy package

description: FIRE (Format for Incident Reporting Exchange) is the Financial Stability Board's common format for cyber incident reporting by financial institutions to authorities, published on 15 April 2025 to streamline incident reporting across jurisdictions. The taxonomy package adds the technical standards for adoption: a data dictionary in the Data Point Model (DPM) method, version 1.0.1 of 23 July 2025 replacing version 1.0, which defines the structured data required for FIRE reports; validation rules that test reported data for consistency; and an XBRL taxonomy so that authorities can collect reports as XBRL-XML or xBRL-CSV, for example through an Excel plug-in. It is produced by the Financial Stability Board. Coverage is global, for any authority that adopts it. The DPM zip, validation rules xlsx and XBRL files are available free to download under the FSB's terms, and XBRL is described as a freely licensed open standard. Caveats: FIRE is a format, not a dataset of incidents, and adoption is voluntary and uneven across jurisdictions. For simulation it defines the fields in which incident impacts, durations and causes are recorded, a template for structuring cyber incident scenarios and event data in resilience models of the financial sector. It is related to the ESAs DORA major ICT incident report record in this catalogue.
